title: Passage and Escarpment
premise: Jonah Iversen, a surveyor who has spent three years hiding her past behind railroad timetables, pulls a sealed chest from the river bearing the crest of a nation that no longer exists—and inside it, documents proving the mountain concession she works under was built on forged permits. Pursued by the railway company's fixer and shadowed by a defector who claims the chest was meant for him, Jonah must cross the escarpment ahead of the early snows to deliver the truth to a border tribunal before the permits legally expire. Along the way she learns that loyalty to the crew who took her in and love for the man hunting her are not opposites but choices. She reaches the pass as the snow closes in, testifies at cost to everyone she cares about, and finally stops measuring life in miles—choosing to stay, visible and accountable, in the valley she once used only as shelter.
about_author: Wren Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent a decade mapping decommissioned rail lines across three continents. They write adventure fiction about people who find belonging in the most inhospitable terrain.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Is Owed
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. During a routine bridge inspection after spring flood, Jonah's crew dredges up an iron chest stamped with the seal of Vessany, a nation dissolved a decade ago. She recognizes the seal from her father's letters. The beat: curiosity curdling into dread as she realizes the past has surfaced whether she wants it or not.

chapters.title: Miles Instead of Years
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Flashback-woven chapter establishing why Jonah measures life in miles: her family's role in the Vessany collapse and her flight into anonymous rail work. Her foreman, Odile, notices the chest has rattled her. Beat: loneliness articulated—the cost of invisibility made explicit.

chapters.title: A Man Who Claims the Water
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Elias Marchetti arrives claiming to be a courier whose shipment went down with a ferry; he knows what's in the chest without being told. Company fixer Harrow arrives the same day asking questions. Beat: attraction and suspicion entwined—Jonah can't tell if Elias is ally, mark, or trap.

chapters.title: What the Seals Say
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, with an interlude letter from Elias. Jonah opens the chest alone: forged concession permits, paymaster ledgers, and names—including her father's. The railway's legal claim to the line expires when the permits do, in six weeks, before the snows. Beat: the weight of proof and the temptation to burn it.

chapters.title: Loyalty Weighs More Than Iron
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The crew's perspective: Odile discovers Jonah's secret but chooses to help, revealing she once lost everything to the same company. They plan the crossing through the escarpment while Harrow tightens surveillance. Beat: chosen family forming—belonging offered freely for the first time.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The crew splits: some carry the documents overland, others run interference on the rails. A rockslide forces them onto a closed line Jonah alone has mapped. Beat: competence as intimacy—Jonah leading, trusting, being trusted back.

chapters.title: Harrow's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Intercepted by Harrow, Elias is offered amnesty and Jonah's ruin in exchange for the ledgers. He stalls, torn between his own duty to the Vessany exiles and the woman he's come to love. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallized—he chooses neither, buying time at great risk.

chapters.title: First Snow on the Pass
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Storm hits early. Harrow's men ambush them at the switchback; Odile is injured covering the retreat, and Jonah must choose between the documents and the people. Beat: climax of values—she refuses the false choice, splitting the party and out-thinking Harrow on her own map.

chapters.title: Testimony at the Border
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. At the tribunal, the permits expire at midnight. Jonah testifies, naming her father among the forgers and herself as heir to that debt. Harrow's counter-evidence collapses when Elias corroborates her. Beat: truth over safety—love against duty resolved not by escape but by standing still and speaking.

chapters.title: Zero Milestone
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Spring. The concession is voided, the crew reorganized under honest charter, Odile recovering. Jonah declines the offer to run far again and instead signs her name to the new survey—first time in three years. Beat: resolution—belonging chosen, identity claimed, the map finally including her.
